main_pathway.description: A single ordered progression of English seed sentences from absolute beginner to comfortably-conversational, covering the highest-frequency, most universally useful things a person needs to say day-to-day. Japanese translations are generated later; register/tags here guide that translation toward casual, natural spoken Japanese rather than textbook phrasing.

sentences.reading: よかったら、いっしょにくる？

sentences.japanese: 気のせいかもしれない。
sentences.reading: きのせいかもしれない。
うまくいけばいいな。

sentences.english: That would be a problem if it happened.
sentences.reading: そうなったらこまるね。

sentences.english: You might wanna bring it just in case.
sentences.japanese: 念のため持ってったほうがいいかも。
sentences.reading: ねんのためもってったほうがいいかも。
sentences.romaji: nen no tame mottetta hou ga ii kamo

sentences.reading: なんとかなるよ。

sentences.english: It's kind of hard to say.
sentences.japanese: ちょっと何とも言えないな。
sentences.reading: ちょっとなんともいえないな。
はんはんくらいだとおもう。

sentences.english: That's probably how it'll turn out, right?
sentences.japanese: たぶんそういうことになるよね？
sentences.reading: たぶんそういうことになるよね？
sentences.romaji: tabun sou iu koto ni naru yo ne

sentences.english: I'll ask, just to be safe.
sentences.reading: ねんのためきいとく。

sentences.english: Worst case, we can just cancel.
sentences.japanese: 最悪、キャンセルすればいいし。
sentences.reading: さいあく、キャンセルすればいいし。

sentences.japanese: それが必ずしも正しいとは限らないよ。
sentences.reading: それがかならずしもただしいとはかぎらないよ。
sentences.romaji: sore ga kanarazushimo tadashii to wa kagiranai yo

sentences.english: No, I don't think that's right.
sentences.japanese: いや、それは違うと思う。
sentences.reading: いや、それはちがうとおもう。
sentences.romaji: iya, sore wa chigau to omou

sentences.english: Isn't that a bit off though?
sentences.context_notes: colloquial, grammatically loose but very common speech pattern intended
sentences.japanese: でもそれ、ちょっと違くない？
sentences.reading: でもそれ、ちょっとちがくない？
sentences.literal_note: Uses the very common colloquial form 違くない instead of the more standard 違わない.

sentences.english: I get how you feel, but...
sentences.reading: きもちはわかるけど…

sentences.english: You've got a point, but still...
sentences.japanese: 言いたいことはわかるけど、それでも…
sentences.reading: いいたいことはわかるけど、それでも…
sentences.romaji: iitai koto wa wakaru kedo, soredemo...

sentences.english: Hmm, I'm not so sure about that.
sentences.japanese: うーん、それはちょっとどうかな。
sentences.reading: うーん、それはちょっとどうかな。
sentences.romaji: uun, sore wa chotto dou kana

sentences.english: I personally think it's fine, though.
sentences.japanese: 個人的には別にいいと思うけど。
sentences.reading: こじんてきにはべつにいいとおもうけど。
sentences.romaji: kojinteki ni wa betsuni ii to omou kedo

sentences.english: Even if you say that, it puts me in a tough spot.
sentences.japanese: そう言われても、こっちも困るんだけど。
sentences.reading: そういわれても、こっちもこまるんだけど。
sentences.romaji: sou iwaretemo, kocchi mo komaru n da kedo

sentences.english: Even if I give you that, still...
sentences.context_notes: reluctant concession before pivoting back to disagreement
sentences.japanese: まあ、そこは認めるとしても、やっぱり…
sentences.reading: まあ、そこはみとめるとしても、やっぱり…
sentences.romaji: maa, soko wa mitomeru to shite mo, yappari...

sentences.english: Isn't that a bit harsh, how you put it?
sentences.japanese: その言い方、ちょっときつくない？
sentences.reading: そのいいかた、ちょっときつくない？

sentences.english: I'm not trying to start a fight or anything.
sentences.japanese: 別にケンカしたいわけじゃないんだけど。
sentences.reading: べつにけんかしたいわけじゃないんだけど。
sentences.romaji: betsuni kenka shitai wake ja nai n da kedo

sentences.reading: はなしずれてきてるよ。

sentences.english: Getting back to what we were saying...
sentences.reading: で、はなしもどすけど…

sentences.english: How about we meet in the middle?
sentences.japanese: 間を取るってのはどう？
sentences.reading: あいだをとるってのはどう？
sentences.romaji: aida o toru tte no wa dou?

sentences.english: Let's just go with that for now.
sentences.japanese: とりあえず今はそれでいこう。
sentences.reading: とりあえずいまはそれでいこう。
sentences.romaji: toriaezu ima wa sore de ikou

sentences.reading: そこはゆずれない。

sentences.japanese: 正直、あんまり納得してない。
sentences.reading: しょうじき、あんまりなっとくしてない。

sentences.english: I get what you're saying, but realistically it's tough.
sentences.japanese: 言いたいことはわかるけど、現実的にはきつい。
sentences.reading: いいたいことはわかるけど、げんじつてきにはきつい。
sentences.romaji: iitai koto wa wakaru kedo, genjitsuteki ni wa kitsui

sentences.english: Well, I guess that's one way to look at it.
sentences.japanese: まあ、そういう見方もあるかもね。
sentences.reading: まあ、そういうみかたもあるかもね。
sentences.romaji: maa, sou iu mikata mo aru kamo ne

sentences.english: Guess I'll just have to give in.
sentences.japanese: もう折れるしかないか。
sentences.reading: もうおれるしかないか。

sentences.english: This'll just go in circles, let's drop it.
sentences.context_notes: refers to a pointless back-and-forth argument
sentences.japanese: これじゃ平行線だし、もうやめよう。
sentences.reading: これじゃへいこうせんだし、もうやめよう。
sentences.romaji: kore ja heikousen da shi, mou yameyou
sentences.literal_note: 平行線 means the discussion is going nowhere, like two parallel lines that never meet.

sentences.context_notes: refers to the cultural concept of reading the atmosphere/mood of a situation
sentences.reading: くうきよんでよ、もう。

sentences.english: Wait, are you actually gonna say that?
sentences.japanese: 待って、それマジで言うの？
sentences.reading: まって、それまじでいうの？
sentences.romaji: matte, sore maji de iu no?

sentences.english: I think I hit a nerve there.
sentences.context_notes: metaphor for accidentally upsetting someone, like stepping on a landmine
sentences.reading: いまの、じらいふんだかも。
sentences.literal_note: 地雷を踏む, literally 'step on a landmine,' is a common metaphor for accidentally touching a sensitive subject.

sentences.english: Honestly, I'm not really feeling it.
sentences.context_notes: expressing true feelings vs. surface-level politeness
sentences.japanese: 正直、あんまり気乗りしない。
sentences.reading: しょうじき、あんまりきのりしない。

sentences.english: Officially/on the surface, that's all I can say.
sentences.context_notes: refers to the honne/tatemae (true feelings vs public stance) cultural concept pair
sentences.japanese: 建前では、それしか言えないかな。
sentences.reading: たてまえでは、それしかいえないかな。
sentences.romaji: tatemae de wa, sore shika ienai kana
sentences.literal_note: 建前 refers to the public or official stance, which may differ from one's true feelings.

sentences.english: You're being pretty roundabout about it.
sentences.japanese: なんか言い方が回りくどいよ。
sentences.reading: なんかいいかたがまわりくどいよ。

sentences.english: You can just be straight with me.
sentences.japanese: 遠慮せずに、はっきり言ってくれていいよ。
sentences.reading: えんりょせずに、はっきりいってくれていいよ。
sentences.romaji: enryo sezu ni, hakkiri itte kurete ii yo

sentences.context_notes: idiom for softening bad news, like wrapping something in a wafer
sentences.japanese: オブラートに包んで言うと…
sentences.reading: おぶらーとにつつんでいうと…
sentences.literal_note: An idiom meaning 'to put it delicately' or soften what you're about to say.

sentences.english: This might be a cynical take, but...
sentences.japanese: ひねくれた見方かもしれないけど…
sentences.reading: ひねくれたみかたかもしれないけど…

sentences.english: That person's kind of sneaky/two-faced, huh.
sentences.context_notes: describes someone secretly scheming, literally 'black-bellied'
sentences.japanese: あの人、けっこう腹黒いよね。
sentences.reading: あのひと、けっこうはらぐろいよね。
sentences.romaji: ano hito, kekkou haraguroi yo ne
sentences.literal_note: 腹黒い literally means 'black-bellied' and refers to someone sneaky, scheming, or two-faced.

sentences.english: I meant it as a joke, but...
I didn't mean any harm by it.
Don't take this the wrong way, okay?
You're reading too much into it.
That's not how I meant it.
There's kind of an implication in how you said that.
We're even, so don't worry about it.

sentences.context_notes: idiom for forgiving and forgetting, literally 'let it flow away in water'

sentences.english: I'm not the type to hold a grudge, so it's fine.
Well, I'll just handle it maturely and let it go.

sentences.context_notes: trendy agreement phrase among younger speakers, roughly 'literally that'

sentences.english: I feel that on a deep level.

sentences.context_notes: used for something emotionally touching, common in fan culture
originally from shogi/chess 'checkmate,' now slang for a hopeless situation

sentences.english: There might be a slim chance.
sentences.context_notes: from English 'one chance,' popular slang for 'maybe, possibly'

sentences.english: That's such a relatable thing, right.
That's an amazing way to handle it.
sentences.context_notes: uses 'god' as slang intensifying prefix meaning 'amazing'
oshi = the person/character you actively support, core fan-culture vocabulary

sentences.english: I fell down the rabbit hole with this.
sentences.context_notes: refers to a deep, hard-to-escape obsession/hobby, literally 'swamp'

sentences.english: They're being really pushy/intense about it.

sentences.context_notes: uses 'resolution' (as in image quality) metaphorically for depth of understanding, trendy tech-adjacent speech

sentences.english: Isn't that just your personal opinion though.
sentences.context_notes: well-known internet meme phrase, often used jokingly to dismiss someone's claim

sentences.english: I'm at a loss for words.
sentences.context_notes: used when something is so impressive/moving you can't describe it

sentences.english: That one line really hit me.
sentences.context_notes: metaphor of piercing/stabbing for something emotionally resonant

sentences.english: That's not how I interpreted the character/story, honestly.
sentences.context_notes: fandom-specific slang for disagreeing with someone's take on a character/story

sentences.english: That's so logically correct I have nothing to say back.
It's basically the very concept of preciousness itself.
sentences.context_notes: playful hyperbolic construction common in enthusiastic fan speech
